{{nihongo|'''Yuge Shrine'''|弓削神社 (八尾市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

{{commons category|Category:Yuge-jinja (Yao, Osaka)}}

``Yuge Shrine'' is located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}. There are two shrines with the same name, both of which are {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi-sha}} ({{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288|lt=Shikiuchi-taisha}}) {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}.

== Overview ==
{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}<ref group="Hara" name="Shinmeicho"/> {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ill|Wakae district|Q11616589|qid=Q11616589}} "Yuge Shrine Niza Dai" There are the following two companies in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}} as {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} of {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi-sha}} ({{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288}}) which is described as ``Monthly Aihan Shinname''.
# '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yuge Shrine}}''' (Yao City {{ill|Higashiyuge|Q11526909|qid=Q11526909}}) - Formerly enshrined in Higashiyuge Village, Wakae District. Old {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.
# '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yuge Shrine}}''' (Yuge Town, Yao City) - Enshrined in the former {{ill|Shiki district|Q11491125|qid=Q11491125}} Nishi Yuge Village (Yuge Village). Old village company.

[[File:Yugedera-ato, zenkei-2.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Yuge-dera|Q28684331|qid=Q28684331}} (Higashiyuge, Yao City)}}]]The two shrines are located approximately 300 meters apart across the {{ill|Nagase River|Q11653384|qid=Q11653384|lt=Nagase River}} {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In the middle {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japanese name book}}" there is a mention of ``Yugego'' in Wakae District, Kawachi Province, and in the Nara period document <ref group="hara">``Shosoin Documents'' August 27, 1986, Tenpyoji 6, ``Zosekizanin Rōgekicho''. </ref> shows ``Yuge Sukune Hakumaro'' as a person from Wakae District, Kawachi Province, so the area is said to have been a settlement of the ancient clan {{ill|Yuge clan|Q11487069|qid=Q11487069}}{{Sfn|Yuge Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Yuge Shrine is said to have been the guardian deity of the Yuge clan from its name, and the location of {{ill|Yuge-dera|Q28684331|qid=Q28684331|lt=Yuge-ji Temple}} (later Yugi-ji Temple), which is said to be the Yuge clan's guardian temple, is also known nearby, and there is also a connection with {{ill|Dōkyō|Q1272718|qid=Q1272718|lt=Yuge Dokyo}}. It is also known that {{ill|Empress Kōken|Q232955|qid=Q232955|lt=Emperor Shotoku}} ran {{ill|Yuge Palace|Q11577605|qid=Q11577605}} (Nishinokyo) in Ren. The area was the domain of {{ill|Taika (era)|Q1077930|qid=Q1077930}}, the former military clan {{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}, and the Yuge clan was the Banzo clan that was under its control and was in charge of Yugebe. group="Hara">``Newly Selected Surnames and Names'' Kamibesu Sakyo Yuge Sukunejo. In </ref>, you can see the description of ``Yuge Sukune'', a second-class member of the {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229|lt=Ibe line}} clan ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenhiwashi Shoya no Mikoto}}) and the Monobe line clan (Ishigami same ancestor). </ref><ref>"Yuge" "Japanese Ancient Clan Encyclopedia New Edition" edited by Arikiyo Saeki, Yuzankaku, 2015. </ref>. In addition, in the Yao City area, there is also the enshrinement of {{ill|Yahagi Shrine, Yao|ja|矢作神社 (八尾市)|qid=Q11583922|lt=Yahagi Shrine}} (Minamihonmachi, Yao City), which is the guardian deity of the Yahagi clan, which was also in charge of the Yahagi club. </ref>, {{ill|Shibukawa Shrine|ja|渋川神社 (八尾市)|qid=Q11561593|lt=Shibukawa Shrine}} (Uematsu-cho, Yao City) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Atobe Shrine}} (Kamei-cho, Yao City) are also known as Mononobe-related shrines.Yuge Shrine is located in ancient Kawachi Province, {{ill|Hiraoka Shrine|abstract|Q32422|de|Hiraoka-Schrein|fr|Hiraoka-jinja|ja|枚岡神社|zh|枚岡神社|qid=Q32422}} ({{ill|Higashiōsaka|ar|هيغاشي-أوساكا (أوساكا)|az|Hiqaşiosaka|ban|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|bg|Хигашиосака|ca|Higashi-Ōsaka|ce|Хигасиосака|ceb|Higashiōsaka Shi|cs|Higašiósaka|cy|Higashiōsaka|de|Higashiōsaka|eo|Higaŝiosaka|es|Higashiōsaka (Osaka)|et|Higashiōsaka|eu|Higashiōsaka|fa|هیگاشی‌اوساکا، اوساکا|fi|Higashi-Ōsaka|fr|Higashiōsaka|ga|Higashiōsaka|gl|Higashiōsaka|he|היגשיאוסקה|hy|Հիգասիոսակա|id|Higashiōsaka|it|Higashiōsaka|ja|東大阪市|ko|히가시오사카시|ms|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|mzn|هیگاشی‌اوساکا، اوساکا|nl|Higashiosaka|no|Higashiōsaka|pl|Higashiōsaka|pt|Higashiosaka|ro|Higashiōsaka|ru|Хигасиосака|sh|Higasiosaka|simple|Higashiōsaka|sr|Хигашиосака|sv|Higashiōsaka|tg|Ҳигашиосака|th|ฮิงาชิโอซากะ|tl|Higashiōsaka|tr|Higashiōsaka|tt|Хигасиосака|tum|Higashiōsaka|uk|Хіґасіосака|ur|ہیگاشیوساکا، اوساکا|vi|Higashiōsaka|war|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|zh|東大阪市|zh_classical|東大阪市|zh_min_nan|Higasiôsaka-chhī|zh_yue|東大阪|qid=Q243863}}, Kawachi Province {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}), {{jali nk|Onchi Shrine|Q11492258}} (Yao City, reportedly Ninomiya, Kawachi Province) is said to be the second most prestigious shrine in the world. However, it has since declined and is now dominated by the two companies listed above. The relationship between the two companies' headquarters and branch offices is not clear, and some theories point out that changes may have occurred due to the village moving or branching off due to flood damage from the {{ill|Yamato River|arz|نهر ياماتو|ceb|Yamato Gawa|es|Río Yamato|fa|رود یاماتو|fr|Yamato-gawa|gl|Río Yamato|it|Yamato (fiume)|ja|大和川|ko|야마토강|ru|Ямато (река)|zh|大和川|qid=Q9001527}}, but this is not clear from historical materials {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In addition, there is a theory that it is assumed that this is the former enshrinement site, as the small letters ``Kogu'' remain in the land approximately 300 meters east of Yuge Shrine in Higashi-Yuge.The details of the two enshrined deities listed in the "Engishiki" divine name book are also unclear, but "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" <ref group="Hara" There is a theory that it is compared to ``Yakafuto no Mikoto'''' and ``Hikosa Jifuto no Mikoto'' (both current locations unknown) in Kawachi Province, which can be seen in name="Jōgan 2-nenjo"/>. In particular, in "Kawachishi", Yuge Shrine in Higashi-Yuge is designated as the god of life of Yakafuto, and Yuge Shrine in Yuge Town is designated as the god of life of Hikosa Jifutto. Shrine (Heibonsha) | 1986}}, this theory is also found in ``Kawachi Meisho Zue'', ``Shinmeichō Kosho'', ``Dainihonshi Jingishi'', and ``Jingishiryo'' {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchisha) | 1979}}. In addition, Yuge Shrine in Yuge Town was called ``Futo Daimyojin'' during the Edo period, and a connection has been pointed out {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. Related articles include "{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}" <ref group="hara">'Kojiki' Jinmu Tennoki. </ref> shows that the sword ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Futomitama}}) given by {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi}} appears to be ``Kafutsujin'' and ``Sashifutsujin'' as alternate names.<ref name="Kafufutsujin">[{{NDLDC|1913359/172}} "Kafutsujin"] "Great Dictionary of Shinto, Volume 3", Heibonsha, 1941 (link to National Diet Library Digital Collection). </ref>.

Founding date is unknown.In {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=National History}}, {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Cheonan}}3rd year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) <ref group="Hara" In the name="Jogan 1st year article"/>, it is written that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of ``Yuge no Kami'' was promoted from the lower rank of junior fifth rank to the higher rank of junior fifth rank {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Also {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}}2 years ({{ill|860|ab|860|af|860|am|860 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|860|ar|860|ary|860|ast|860|avk|860|az|860|azb|۸۶۰ (میلادی)|ban|860|bar|860|bcl|860|be|860|be_x_old|860|bg|860|bn|৮৬০|bpy|মারি ৮৬০|br|860|bs|860.|ca|860|cdo|860 nièng|ceb|860|ckb|٨٦٠|crh|860|cs|860|csb|860|cv|860|cy|860|da|860|de|860|el|860|eml|860|eo|860|es|860|et|860|eu|860|fa|۸۶۰ (میلادی)|fi|860|fo|860|fr|860|fy|860|ga|860|gan|860年|gd|860|gl|860|he|860|hi|860|hr|860.|ht|860 (almanak jilyen)|hu|860|hy|860|id|860|ilo|860|io|860|is|860|it|860|ja|860年|jv|860|ka|860|kaa|860|kk|860 жыл|ko|860년|la|860|lb|860|lij|860|lmo|860|lt|860 m.|lv|860. gads|map_bms|860|mdf|860|mg|860|mhr|860|mk|860|mr|इ.स. ८६०|mrj|860 и|ms|860|mzn|۸۶۰|nah|860|nap|860|nds|860|new|सन् ८६०|nl|860|nn|860|no|860|nrm|860|nso|860|oc|860|or|୮୬୦|os|860-æм аз|pl|860|pnb|860|pt|860|qu|860|ro|860|ru|860 год|rue|860|sa|८६०|scn|860|sd|860ع|se|860|sh|860.|shn|860|si|860|simple|860|sk|860|sl|860|smn|860|sq|860|sr|860|su|860|sv|860|sw|860|tg|Соли 860|th|พ.ศ. 1403|tk|860|tl|860|tly|860|tr|860|tt|860 ел|uk|860|ur|860ء|uz|860|vec|860|vi|860|war|860|wuu|860年|xmf|860|zh|860年|zh_min_nan|860 nî|zh_yue|860年|qid=Q24714}})<ref group="Hara" name="Jogan 2nd Year Article"/>There is a theory that it is compared to ``Yakafuto no Mikoto'' and ``Hikosa Jifuto no Mikoto'' of Kawachi Province, who appear to have progressed from Junior Third Rank to Junior Second Rank. However, since it is a much higher divine rank than Jugoi-jo (Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Rank) in the 3rd year of Tenan, there are strong negative opinions {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}<ref group="Hara" name="Shinmyocho">"Engishiki" Volume 9 (Shinmyo 1) Wakae District, Kawachi Province. </ref>, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ill|Wakae district|Q11616589|qid=Q11616589}} has "Yuge Shrine Niza Dai As part of the "Monthly Aijo Niiname", two troupes were placed in {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288|lt=Shikiuchi Taisha}}, and the {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11516161}} and {{jalin k|Ainamesai|Q11581944}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}, it is stipulated that it is kept in a heihaku {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikinaisha)|1979}}. According to a note in the Kongoji book, it is said to have already existed at the ``{{ill|Kōnin-shiki|Q17228444|qid=Q17228444}}'' stage {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. In addition, in Kawachi Province, only three shrines were preserved for the Aiga Festival: {{ill|Hiraoka Shrine|abstract|Q32422|de|Hiraoka-Schrein|fr|Hiraoka-jinja|ja|枚岡神社|zh|枚岡神社|qid=Q32422}} ({{ill|Higashiōsaka|ar|هيغاشي-أوساكا (أوساكا)|az|Hiqaşiosaka|ban|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|bg|Хигашиосака|ca|Higashi-Ōsaka|ce|Хигасиосака|ceb|Higashiōsaka Shi|cs|Higašiósaka|cy|Higashiōsaka|de|Higashiōsaka|eo|Higaŝiosaka|es|Higashiōsaka (Osaka)|et|Higashiōsaka|eu|Higashiōsaka|fa|هیگاشی‌اوساکا، اوساکا|fi|Higashi-Ōsaka|fr|Higashiōsaka|ga|Higashiōsaka|gl|Higashiōsaka|he|היגשיאוסקה|hy|Հիգասիոսակա|id|Higashiōsaka|it|Higashiōsaka|ja|東大阪市|ko|히가시오사카시|ms|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|mzn|هیگاشی‌اوساکا، اوساکا|nl|Higashiosaka|no|Higashiōsaka|pl|Higashiōsaka|pt|Higashiosaka|ro|Higashiōsaka|ru|Хигасиосака|sh|Higasiosaka|simple|Higashiōsaka|sr|Хигашиосака|sv|Higashiōsaka|tg|Ҳигашиосака|th|ฮิงาชิโอซากะ|tl|Higashiōsaka|tr|Higashiōsaka|tt|Хигасиосака|tum|Higashiōsaka|uk|Хіґасіосака|ur|ہیگاشیوساکا، اوساکا|vi|Higashiōsaka|war|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|zh|東大阪市|zh_classical|東大阪市|zh_min_nan|Higasiôsaka-chhī|zh_yue|東大阪|qid=Q243863}}), {{ill|Onji Shrine|ja|恩智神社|qid=Q11492258}} (Yao City), and Yuge Shrine. According to the Shinmeicho, Yuge Shrines are also known to exist in {{ill|Kai Province|ckb|پارێزگای کای|cs|Provincie Kai|de|Provinz Kai|eo|Provinco Kai|es|Provincia de Kai|eu|Kai probintzia|fa|ولایت کای|fi|Kain provinssi|fr|Province de Kai|gl|Provincia de Kai|id|Provinsi Kai|it|Kai (provincia)|ja|甲斐国|ko|가이국|lt|Kajaus žemė|ms|Wilayah Kai|nl|Kai (provincie)|pt|Província de Kai|ru|Каи (провинция)|simple|Kai Province|sk|Kai (provincia)|sr|Провинција Каи|tr|Kai (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кай|wuu|甲斐国|zh|甲斐國|zh_min_nan|Kai-kok|zh_yue|甲斐國|qid=Q858076}}{{ill|Yatsushiro District, Kumamoto|Q1043800|qid=Q1043800}} and {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}{{ill|Takashima District, Shiga|Q11669692|qid=Q11669692|lt=Takashima District}}.{{ill|Eiman|Q1193868|qid=Q1193868}} In June 1st year ({{ill|1165|Q19676|qid=Q19676}}), in the ``Annual Tribute Order for Shrines and Shrines'', it is listed as ``Yugesha {{sub|Shinbutsu Kosei}}'' along with Hiraoka-sha and Onchi-sha.{{Sfn|Yuge-jinja (Heibon-sha)|1986}}.

The changes during the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} period are not clear. {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} In the ``Kanshin-ji Annual Revised Kanjo Jinmyocho'' of 20 years ({{ill|1551|Q6560|qid=Q6560}}), it appears as ``Yuge Daimyojin'' {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

In the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} period, one shrine each was enshrined in Higashi-Yuge and Nishi-Yuge, as they are today {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, both Higashi-Yuge and Nishi-Yuge were established in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}) {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikinai Shrine) |1979}} is ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.

== God level ==
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from the lower junior fifth rank to the upper junior fifth rank ("{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}") <ref group="Hara" name="Jogan 1st year article">New Year 27th article of the 1st year of Jogan (859) in "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku". </ref> - The notation is "Yugegami".
{{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}}2 years ({{ill|860|ab|860|af|860|am|860 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|860|ar|860|ary|860|ast|860|avk|860|az|860|azb|۸۶۰ (میلادی)|ban|860|bar|860|bcl|860|be|860|be_x_old|860|bg|860|bn|৮৬০|bpy|মারি ৮৬০|br|860|bs|860.|ca|860|cdo|860 nièng|ceb|860|ckb|٨٦٠|crh|860|cs|860|csb|860|cv|860|cy|860|da|860|de|860|el|860|eml|860|eo|860|es|860|et|860|eu|860|fa|۸۶۰ (میلادی)|fi|860|fo|860|fr|860|fy|860|ga|860|gan|860年|gd|860|gl|860|he|860|hi|860|hr|860.|ht|860 (almanak jilyen)|hu|860|hy|860|id|860|ilo|860|io|860|is|860|it|860|ja|860年|jv|860|ka|860|kaa|860|kk|860 жыл|ko|860년|la|860|lb|860|lij|860|lmo|860|lt|860 m.|lv|860. gads|map_bms|860|mdf|860|mg|860|mhr|860|mk|860|mr|इ.स. ८६०|mrj|860 и|ms|860|mzn|۸۶۰|nah|860|nap|860|nds|860|new|सन् ८६०|nl|860|nn|860|no|860|nrm|860|nso|860|oc|860|or|୮୬୦|os|860-æм аз|pl|860|pnb|860|pt|860|qu|860|ro|860|ru|860 год|rue|860|sa|८६०|scn|860|sd|860ع|se|860|sh|860.|shn|860|si|860|simple|860|sk|860|sl|860|smn|860|sq|860|sr|860|su|860|sv|860|sw|860|tg|Соли 860|th|พ.ศ. 1403|tk|860|tl|860|tly|860|tr|860|tt|860 ел|uk|860|ur|860ء|uz|860|vec|860|vi|860|war|860|wuu|860年|xmf|860|zh|860年|zh_min_nan|860 nî|zh_yue|860年|qid=Q24714}}) <ref group="Hara" name="Jokan 2 years article"> "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" July 10th year of the 2nd year of Jogan (860). </ref>There is a theory that the ``Yakafuto no Mikoto'' and ``Hikosa Jifuto no Mikoto'' of Kawachi Province, who progressed from Junior Third Rank to Junior Second Rank, are related to our company {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1 979}}{{Sfn|Yuge Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}} (There is also a theory that it is compared to 2 of the 4 dais of Hiraoka Shrine {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine 2 za (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}).

== History ==
"Yugejin" in "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) article (Era name)|Q1327274|Extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}<ref group="Hara" {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine) |1979}} is said to be {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} of {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288|lt=Shikiuchi Taisha}} in name="Shinmeicho"/>.

== History ==
"Yugejin" in "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) article (Era name)|Q1327274|Extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}<ref group="Hara" {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine) |1979}} is said to be {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} of {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288|lt=Shikiuchi Taisha}} in name="Shinmeicho"/>.

In "Kawachishi" and "Kawachi Kanmeishoki", it appears as "Daimyojin of Yawata Kasuga Gozu Tenno Prefectural Capital" {{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}) nk|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534}}, it is ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}{{Sfn|Yuge Shrine Niza (shikinaisha)|1979}}.

== Festival ==
The main festivals held during the year are as follows <ref> Yuge Shrine (Yuge Town) Precinct Explanation Board. </ref>.
* New Year's Day Festival ({{ill|January 1|Q2150|qid=Q2150}})
* Prayer Festival ({{ill|February 17|Q2341|qid=Q2341}})
* <s>Summer Festival ({{ill|July 31|Q2715|qid=Q2715}})</s>→Integrated into Autumn Festival
* Autumn festival <ref>{{Cite web |title=Shikiyuge Neighborhood Association Federation |url=https://shikiyuge2019.com/ |website=Shikiyuge Neighborhood Association Federation |access-date=2025-07-06 |language=ja}}</ref> ({{ill|October 9|Q2923|qid=Q2923}}) Saturday and Sunday in late September or the first week of October
* New Grain Thanksgiving ({{ill|November 23|Q3021|qid=Q3021}})
